attacks.title: 150 hostile slice id runs on patch-slice and base-branch
attacks.result: no traceback, all refused or answered, base-branch tree unchanged

seeds.title: patch-slice makes and checks out a branch for an unknown slice id
seeds.detail: ensure_slice_branch runs before the slice lookup, so patch-slice with an id absent from slices.json creates feature/PROJ-1-<id> and leaves HEAD on it, then refuses. Same order as before the slice (old code made sdlc/<id>). Seen with ids such as /etc, S-٣, -1.

seeds.title: state-write does not validate a format for git safety
seeds.detail: branchFormat values such as 'has space/{name}', 'x~/{name}', '/{name}', 'a/{name}.lock' and '{x}/{name}' reach git. base-branch prints an invalid name with exit 0. patch-slice returns the raw git error as JSON, exit 2, and changes nothing. Format '{x}/{name}' is accepted. branches.validate_format already rejects these but state-write does not call it.

seeds.title: non-string or empty branchFormat falls back to the default silently
seeds.detail: branchFormat 5 or ["a"] gives sdlc/ names with no warning. This matches load_format semantics in the spec. No repo-level format file exists in this version, so the plan note about a repo file does not apply.

seeds.title: prune treats M-0, leading zeros and non-ASCII digits as milestone ids
seeds.detail: The parse pattern uses \d on str, so feature/PROJ-1-M-٣ counts as a shipped milestone branch and is deleted. The old regex behaved the same, so this is parity, not a regression.
